title: Auto Loans: Combined Auto Lending Exposure Limit
content:
Auto Loans lending at Piedmont Crescent Bank is aggregated per borrower, and the aggregate is held to a single dollar limit that is tested both when an application is recorded and when a loan is funded.

## Rule

The borrower's auto exposure, taken together with the amount now requested, may not exceed 175000.00 US dollars. Auto exposure means:

- the unpaid principal of each of the borrower's auto loans that is active or delinquent; plus
- the amount requested on each of the borrower's applications still in applied status.

Paid-off loans never enter the figure. The test uses the bank's loan records for the borrower, read at the moment of the application or of the funding. It concerns lending volume only: discounts, rates and fees continue to be decided loan by loan and are never worked out on combined balances.

## How the figure is built

| Record on the borrower's file | Amount taken into exposure |
|---|---|
| Active loan | its unpaid principal |
| Delinquent loan | its unpaid principal |
| Application in applied status | the amount requested on it |
| Paid-off loan | nothing |
| The request under consideration | the amount requested, added on top |

## Boundary illustration (hypothetical balances)

A borrower has an active loan with 60000.00 of unpaid principal and a pending application for 40000.00. A further request of 75000.00 brings the total to 175000.00, which does not exceed the limit and so passes. A further request of 75000.01 would bring it to 175000.01 and fail. Had the first loan been paid off, it would contribute nothing and the same request would leave ample room. All balances here are invented for the illustration.
